content.text: Minobasco (often associated with the name 'Shokoba') is a specialized, modern variant of the traditional Italian fishing game 'Escoba' (or Scopa). It is unique for its use of colorful plastic 'Gemstones' as scoring tokens and its simplified point-capture rules aimed at a faster, more competitive pace. Like Scopa, players use cards from their hand to capture sums of cards from the table, but with an emphasis on 'Shokoba'â€”clearing the entire table for a bonus point.
A modern evolution of 'Escoba de 15' (Spanish/Italian fishing). The 'Minobasco' branding emerged in Central Europe (Liechtenstein/Switzerland) as a boutique card set in the late 20th century.
Each player receives 3 cards. 4 cards are placed face-up on the table. The deal is repeated until the deck is empty.

items.text: Standard Minobasco: Two to four players; capture by value or sum; Shokoba (sweep) awards 1 Gemstone; first to 11 Gemstones wins.
Scopa (Italian): Parent game; same capture and sweep rules, scored with traditional Scopa points (cards, coins, settebello, primiera, scope).
Team play (4 players): Four players in two teams; partners sit opposite; same rules, team score first to 11 Gemstones.
